# Overview

**Module 5: Allele structure**

This module looks at the sequence of the reads around the primary tract:

1. **Allele clustering** (cluster = `r params$cluster`): reads are grouped by repeat length (`r paste(params$cluster_by, collapse = " then ")`), clustered on `r resolve_cluster_unit(params$cluster_unit, params$umi, isTRUE(params$umi) && file.exists(file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "04_umi.RData")))` (`cluster_unit`; with molecules, each kept UMI molecule's length is clustered and its reads take its cluster). The number of length clusters is chosen by a Gaussian mixture, and clusters holding under `r percent(params$repeat_cluster_min_prop)` of a sample's reads are merged into their neighbour, so an expansion smear is not cut into many small clusters. With `haplotype` in `cluster_by`, reads are also grouped by flank haplotype: 15-mers found in 10–90% of reads are kept only when at least 7 others appear in exactly the same reads (the signature of a real SNP or indel, not a sequencing error), they are grouped into variant blocks, and each read is scored on the k-mers it carries from each allele of each block. A split is accepted when the mean silhouette exceeds 0.5 and every cluster holds at least 5% of reads, so haplotypes carried by more than about 10–20% of reads are found. Reads whose flank variants combine the two alleles' haplotypes (e.g. PCR chimeras) form their own cluster
2. **Alleles.** In each sample, the two clusters with the most reads (molecules, when clustered on molecules) are its **alleles 1 and 2**, numbered by the length of the primary tract (allele 1 = the shorter); any further clusters (a subclone, PCR chimeras) are numbered 3 upwards by reads
3. **Consensus sequences** of each allele's left flank, tract and right flank (DECIPHER, up to `r params$consensus_downsample` reads, `r percent(params$consensus_threshold)` agreement; the tract consensus uses only reads at the allele's modal length), joined into one full-length allele sequence; the region between the reference flanks is written in repeat notation, e.g. (CAG)17 CAACAGCCGCCA (CCG)7
4. **Phased variants**: each allele's flank consensus against the reference (so every variant belongs to allele 1 or 2), plus substitutions carried by at least `r if (is.na(params$allele_minor_share)) "– (off)" else percent(params$allele_minor_share)` of an allele's reads but not in its consensus; for each, the share of the allele's reads that carry it (its **read support**)
5. **Standard files**: a phased VCF with one column per sample (the repeat region as one record with each allele's motif counts, and the flank variants with their read support per allele), the allele sequences as FASTA, and `r if (isTRUE(params$allele_bam)) "a BAM per sample of reads aligned to the whole reference and tagged by allele (HP), for IGV" else "no BAMs (allele_bam = FALSE)"`
6. **Waterfall plots** (waterfall = `r params$waterfall`): reads stacked by repeat length with each base coloured, `r params$waterfall_flank_bp` bp of flank either side of the tract

**Outputs** (as in every module, tables and data files are at the top of the module's folder, figures under `plots/`):

- `05_allele_structure/allele_structure.xlsx` – clusters, alleles (lengths of every measure, repeat notation, sequences), variants with read support
- `05_allele_structure/consensus/alleles.fasta` – one full-length sequence per allele (with `consensus_parts = TRUE`, the left, tract and right parts in their own files too)
- `05_allele_structure/variants/alleles.vcf` (and `.vcf.gz` with a tabix index where bgzip and tabix are installed) – phased, one column per sample
- `05_allele_structure/bam/{sample}.bam` – reads aligned to the reference, tagged HP (allele), XR (primary repeat length) and, with UMIs, MI (molecule). BAMs are often left out when results are copied from a cluster (e.g. `rsync --exclude '*.bam'`); copy this folder if you want to view the alleles in IGV
- `05_allele_structure/plots/alleles/alleles_{sample}.png` – each sample's alleles and variants
- `05_allele_structure/plots/clusters/clusters_{sample}.png` – each sample's reads by cluster
- `05_allele_structure/plots/waterfall/waterfall_{sample}.png` (and `waterfall_cluster/` when selected in `plots`)

# Allele clustering

`r if (!params$cluster) "**Not run** (\u0060cluster = FALSE\u0060, the default). Set \u0060--cluster TRUE\u0060 to group reads into alleles, build consensus sequences and call flank variants." else ""`

```{r clustering, eval=params$cluster}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
# With UMIs, lengths are clustered per molecule (one consensus length per kept molecule, so
# PCR copies and PCR-shortened reads do not weigh in) and each read takes its molecule's
# cluster; reads not in a kept molecule are left out, as they are from the molecule-level
# instability metrics. Without UMIs, each read's own length is clustered.
cluster_unit <- resolve_cluster_unit(params$cluster_unit, params$umi, !is.null(read_mol))
mol_len <- NULL
if (cluster_unit == "molecules") {
  safe_load_module(m4, 4)
  mol_len <- module4_output$molecules[kept == TRUE & is.finite(primary_length), .(file_stem, molecule_id, mol_length = primary_length)]
  mol_measures <- module4_output$molecule_lengths[, .(file_stem, molecule_id, measure, length)]   # every measure, kept molecules
  rm(module4_output); invisible(gc())
  d_all <- mol_len[read_mol, on = .(file_stem, molecule_id), nomatch = NULL][, .(file_stem, qname, molecule_id, mol_length)][d_all, on = .(file_stem, qname)]
  no_molecule <- d_all[is.na(molecule_id), .(reads = .N), by = file_stem]
  d_all <- d_all[!is.na(molecule_id)]
}
per_sample <- split(d_all, by = "file_stem")
clusters <- rbindlist(apply_fn(names(per_sample), function(s) {
  cache <- file.path(temp_dir, paste0("cluster_v332_", cluster_unit, "_", s, ".RData"))
  if (safe_load_cache(cache, environment())) return(res)
  d <- per_sample[[s]]
  rc <- NULL
  if (cluster_unit == "molecules" && "repeat" %in% params$cluster_by) {
    m <- unique(d[, .(molecule_id, mol_length)])
    m[, rc := cluster_by_repeat_length(mol_length, params$repeat_cluster_max, params$repeat_cluster_min_prop, params$repeat_cluster_downsample)]
    rc <- m$rc[match(d$molecule_id, m$molecule_id)]
    rc[!is.finite(d$length)] <- NA_integer_   # no tract in this read: R0, as without UMIs
  }
  res <- cbind(d[, .(file_stem, qname)], cluster_sample(as.data.frame(d), params, rc = rc))
  save(res, file = cache); res
}))
d_all <- clusters[d_all, on = .(file_stem, qname)]
# Reads where no tract was found have no length to cluster on; they are counted
# here and left out of the clusters, consensus and waterfalls
no_tract <- d_all[repeat_cluster == "R0", .(reads = .N), by = file_stem]
d_all <- d_all[repeat_cluster != "R0"]
d_all[, cluster_number := match(cluster_number, sort(unique(cluster_number))), by = file_stem]
# Length statistics of each cluster: over its molecules (one length per molecule) when
# clustering was on molecules, so they describe the length interval that was clustered;
# otherwise over its reads
stat_src <- if (cluster_unit == "molecules") unique(d_all[, .(file_stem, cluster_number, molecule_id, length = mol_length)], by = c("file_stem", "molecule_id")) else d_all
cluster_summary <- stat_src[, .(modal_length = { tb <- table(length); as.numeric(names(tb)[which.max(tb)]) },
                             median_length = as.numeric(median(length)), mean_length = mean(length), sd_length = sd(length),
                             p10_length = as.numeric(stats::quantile(length, 0.1)), p90_length = as.numeric(stats::quantile(length, 0.9))),
                         by = .(file_stem, cluster_number)]
cluster_summary <- d_all[, .(reads = .N, molecules = if ("molecule_id" %in% names(d_all)) uniqueN(molecule_id) else NA_integer_,
                             repeat_cluster = repeat_cluster[1], haplotype_cluster = haplotype_cluster[1]),
                         by = .(file_stem, cluster_number)][cluster_summary, on = .(file_stem, cluster_number)]
cluster_summary[, length_stats_from := cluster_unit]
cluster_summary[, proportion := reads / sum(reads), by = file_stem]
setorder(cluster_summary, file_stem, cluster_number)
# Alleles 1 and 2 = the two clusters with most reads, numbered by length (1 = shorter);
# any other cluster is 3, 4, ... by reads
# (by molecules when clustering was on molecules: PCR copies would otherwise favour
# whichever allele amplified best)
cluster_summary[, molecule_proportion := molecules / sum(molecules), by = file_stem]
cluster_summary[, size := if (cluster_unit == "molecules") molecules else reads]
cluster_summary[, rank_reads := frank(-size, ties.method = "first"), by = file_stem]
cluster_summary[rank_reads <= 2, allele := frank(modal_length, ties.method = "first"), by = file_stem]
cluster_summary[rank_reads > 2, allele := 2L + frank(-size, ties.method = "first"), by = file_stem]
cluster_summary[, size := NULL]
cluster_summary[, rank_reads := NULL]
timings["Clustering"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

`r if (params$cluster) { if (cluster_unit == "molecules") sprintf("**Clustered on molecules.** Each kept molecule's %s length (its consensus over its reads, Module 4) is clustered, and every read takes its molecule's cluster, so PCR copies of one molecule count once and PCR-shortened reads do not pull the clusters about. %s reads not in a kept molecule (no UMI, or a molecule dropped in Module 4) are left out of the clusters, consensus and waterfalls. Set \u0060cluster_unit = reads\u0060 to cluster each read's own length instead.", primary, format(sum(no_molecule$reads), big.mark = ",")) else "**Clustered on reads**: each read's own length is clustered." } else ""`

`r if (params$cluster && exists("no_tract") && nrow(no_tract)) sprintf("%s reads in %d samples had no %s tract to measure and are left out of the clusters, consensus and waterfalls (at most %s in one sample).", format(sum(no_tract$reads), big.mark = ","), nrow(no_tract), primary, format(max(no_tract$reads), big.mark = ",")) else ""`


`r if (params$cluster) paste0("## Clusters in every sample\n\n**How to read this.** One row per sample. Each cluster is a horizontal line from the 10th to the 90th percentile of its " , if (exists("cluster_unit") && cluster_unit == "molecules") "molecules'" else "reads'", " lengths, with a point at its modal length; the size of the point is the cluster's share of the sample's ", if (exists("cluster_unit") && cluster_unit == "molecules") "molecules" else "reads", ", and the colour its order by length within the sample (1 = shortest), so the same allele has the same colour in every sample (the cluster numbers in the table count from the cluster with most reads, which can differ between samples). Clusters with the same length in every sample are the same allele across the cohort; a cluster that appears in only some samples, or whose length moves between samples, is where to look.") else ""`

```{r cluster_overview, eval=params$cluster, fig.height=min(30, max(4, 2 + 0.16 * length(samples)))}
lab_c <- short_labels(cluster_summary$file_stem)
co <- copy(cluster_summary)[, sample := factor(lab_c[file_stem], levels = rev(unique(lab_c[sort(unique(file_stem))])))]
# Coloured by length order within the sample (1 = shortest), which means the same allele
# across samples, unlike the cluster number (1 = most reads), which can swap between samples
co[, order := factor(frank(modal_length, ties.method = "first")), by = file_stem]
p_co <- ggplot(co, aes(y = sample, colour = order)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = p10_length, xend = p90_length, yend = sample), linewidth = 0.6, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(x = modal_length, size = if (cluster_unit == "molecules") molecule_proportion else proportion)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 4, labels = pct_axis(), name = paste0("Share of\nthe sample's\n", cluster_unit)) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Cluster, by length\n(1 = shortest)") +
  labs(x = paste(primary, "length (repeat units)"), y = NULL, title = "Clusters in every sample",
       subtitle = sprintf("Point = modal length; line = 10th to 90th percentile of the cluster's %s", cluster_unit)) +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = if (length(samples) > 60) 5 else 8))
print(p_co); save_plot(p_co, file.path(plots_dir, "clusters_overview.png"), 10, min(45, max(4, 2 + 0.16 * length(samples))))
```

`r if (params$cluster) "## Allele shares in every sample" else ""`

`r if (params$cluster) "How each sample's reads (and, with UMIs, its molecules) split between its alleles: allele 1 (red, the shorter of the two largest clusters, coloured as in the other cluster figures), allele 2 (blue) and any extra clusters (grey). A sample should give one cluster per allele it carries (two for a heterozygous sample, as the subtitle counts); grey usually means an allele with a wide length distribution (often an expanded one) or a mixture of cells or samples. A share far from 50% is allelic imbalance; when the read share of the expanded allele is lower than its molecule share, the longer allele amplified or sequenced less well, which counting molecules corrects." else ""`

```{r cluster_count, eval=params$cluster, fig.height=min(30, max(4, 2.2 + 0.18 * length(samples)))}
# Share of each sample's reads (and, with UMIs, molecules) in allele 1, allele 2 and any
# extra alleles, so an unbalanced or extra allele stands out sample by sample
nclu <- cluster_summary[, .N, by = file_stem]
lab_s <- short_labels(cluster_summary$file_stem)
sh_units <- c(reads = "reads", if (cluster_unit == "molecules") c(molecules = "molecules"))
sh <- rbindlist(lapply(names(sh_units), function(u) cluster_summary[, .(file_stem, allele, n = get(u), unit = u)]))
sh[, share := n / sum(n), by = .(file_stem, unit)]
sh[, allele_lab := factor(ifelse(allele <= 2, paste("Allele", allele), "Extra alleles (3+)"), levels = c("Extra alleles (3+)", "Allele 2", "Allele 1"))]
sh <- sh[, .(share = sum(share)), by = .(file_stem, unit, allele_lab)]
sh[, sample := factor(lab_s[file_stem], levels = rev(unique(lab_s[sort(unique(file_stem))])))]
sh[, unit := factor(paste("Share of", unit), levels = paste("Share of", names(sh_units)))]
p_cc <- ggplot(sh, aes(x = share, y = sample, fill = allele_lab)) + geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(data = sh[share >= 0.08], aes(label = scales::percent(share, 1)), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), colour = "white", size = if (length(samples) > 40) 2 else 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey40", linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~ unit, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Allele 1` = "#e41a1c", `Allele 2` = "#377eb8", `Extra alleles (3+)` = "grey60"), name = NULL, breaks = c("Allele 1", "Allele 2", "Extra alleles (3+)")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = paste0("How each sample's ", if (length(sh_units) > 1) "reads and molecules split" else "reads split", " between its alleles"),
       subtitle = paste0("Allele 1 = the shorter of the two largest clusters. ",
                         paste(sprintf("%d samples with %d cluster%s", as.integer(table(nclu$N)), as.integer(names(table(nclu$N))), ifelse(names(table(nclu$N)) == "1", "", "s")), collapse = "; "))) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.spacing = unit(1.5, "lines"), axis.text.y = element_text(size = if (length(samples) > 60) 5 else 8))
print(p_cc); save_plot(p_cc, plot_path(plots_dir, "allele_shares"), 4 + 3 * length(sh_units), min(45, max(4, 2.2 + 0.18 * length(samples))))
```

`r if (params$cluster) paste0("## One sample's clusters\n\nThe lengths that were clustered in one sample (", if (cluster_unit == "molecules") "one per UMI molecule, so PCR-shortened reads do not smear the clusters" else "one per read", "), one row per cluster on a shared length axis, so each cluster's length distribution can be seen even where clusters overlap. In grey behind each row are all the sample's lengths, so each row shows which part of the distribution its cluster took and where the split between clusters fell. Each row gives the cluster's allele number (1 and 2 are the two largest clusters, 1 the shorter; 3 upwards are the rest), modal length and share of ", cluster_unit, ". Where the sample's reads were also split by flank haplotype, the row says which: haplotypes are numbered separately within each length cluster, so H2 in one row is not the same sequence as H2 in another. Two clusters with the same modal length and different haplotypes are reads of the same length whose flanks differ; the allele table (*Alleles in every sample*) says whose flanks each extra cluster carries. Every sample is in \u0060plots/clusters/clusters_{sample}.png\u0060.") else ""`

```{r cluster_example, eval=params$cluster, fig.height=if (exists("cluster_summary")) 1.8 + 1.3 * nrow(cluster_summary[file_stem == samples[1]]) else 4.5}
cl_dir <- file.path(plots_dir, "clusters")
for (s in samples) {
  if (s != samples[1] && !want_plot("clusters", params)) break
  p <- cluster_length_plot(d_all[file_stem == s], cluster_summary[file_stem == s], s, paste(primary, "length (repeat units)"), clustered_on = cluster_unit)
  if (s == samples[1]) print(p)
  save_plot(p, plot_path(plots_dir, "clusters", s), 10, 1.8 + 1.3 * nrow(cluster_summary[file_stem == s]))
}
dt_full(cluster_summary, caption = "Clusters per sample (cluster 1 = most reads)", digits = 3)
```

# Alleles, consensus and variants

`r if (!params$cluster) "**Not run** (needs cluster = TRUE)." else ""`

```{r alleles_assign, eval=params$cluster}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
d_all <- cluster_summary[, .(file_stem, cluster_number, allele)][d_all, on = .(file_stem, cluster_number)]
left_ref <- substr(ref$full, 1, ref$n_start - 1); right_ref <- substr(ref$full, ref$n_end + 1, nchar(ref$full))
```

```{r consensus, eval=params$cluster}
keys <- cluster_summary[, .(file_stem, cluster_number, allele)]
minor_share <- if (isTRUE(params$call_variants)) params$allele_minor_share else NA
cons <- rbindlist(apply_fn(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
  s <- keys$file_stem[i]; k <- keys$cluster_number[i]
  cache <- file.path(temp_dir, paste0("consensus_v333_", s, "_", k, ".RData"))
  if (safe_load_cache(cache, environment())) return(res)
  d <- d_all[file_stem == s & cluster_number == k]
  cl <- consensus_function(d$left, params$consensus_threshold, params$consensus_downsample, minor_share)
  # the tract consensus comes from reads at the allele's modal length (the modal
  # molecule length when clustering was on molecules), so it shows the structure of
  # that allele rather than a blend of lengths
  tb <- table(if ("mol_length" %in% names(d)) unique(d[, .(molecule_id, mol_length)])$mol_length else d$length)
  dm <- if (length(tb)) d[length == as.numeric(names(tb)[which.max(tb)])] else d
  if (!nrow(dm)) dm <- d
  # ... and of those, the reads whose whole region between the flanks has its commonest
  # length (another tract, such as CCG, can differ), so the reads are in register and are
  # combined column by column rather than aligned
  if (nrow(dm) > 1) { nb <- table(nchar(dm$mid)); dm <- dm[nchar(mid) == as.integer(names(nb)[which.max(nb)])] }
  cm <- consensus_function(dm$mid, params$consensus_threshold, params$consensus_downsample)
  cr <- consensus_function(d$right, params$consensus_threshold, params$consensus_downsample, minor_share)
  res <- data.table(file_stem = s, cluster_number = k, reads_for_consensus = cm$n,
                    consensus_left = cl$consensus, consensus_mid = cm$consensus, consensus_right = cr$consensus,
                    minor_left = list(cl$minor), minor_right = list(cr$minor))
  save(res, file = cache); res
}))
cons <- cluster_summary[, .(file_stem, cluster_number, allele, reads, proportion, molecules, molecule_proportion, modal_length)][cons, on = .(file_stem, cluster_number)]
setorder(cons, file_stem, allele)
# The region between the reference flanks, in repeat notation, and how much flank the consensus covers
bf <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(cons)), function(i) between_flanks(cons$consensus_left[i], cons$consensus_mid[i], cons$consensus_right[i], left_ref, right_ref, ref$n_end))
cons[, `:=`(repeat_sequence = vapply(bf, `[[`, "", "sequence"), left_from = vapply(bf, function(b) as.numeric(b$left_from), 0), right_to = vapply(bf, function(b) as.numeric(b$right_to), 0))]
cons[, repeat_notation := vapply(repeat_sequence, repeat_notation, "", motifs = tracts$motif)]
cons[, full_sequence := paste0(fifelse(is.na(consensus_left), "", consensus_left), fifelse(is.na(consensus_mid), "", consensus_mid), fifelse(is.na(consensus_right), "", consensus_right))]
# Modal length of every measure (tract or combined) in each allele: over its molecules
# when clustering was on molecules (as the cluster table), otherwise over its reads
al_len <- if (cluster_unit == "molecules") unique(d_all[, .(file_stem, molecule_id, allele)], by = c("file_stem", "molecule_id"))[mol_measures, on = .(file_stem, molecule_id), nomatch = NULL] else
  d_all[, .(file_stem, qname, allele)][read_lengths, on = .(file_stem, qname), nomatch = NULL]
al_mod <- al_len[, .(modal = { tb <- table(length); as.numeric(names(tb)[which.max(tb)]) }), by = .(file_stem, allele, measure)]
al_wide <- dcast(al_mod, file_stem + allele ~ measure, value.var = "modal")
setnames(al_wide, setdiff(names(al_wide), c("file_stem", "allele")), paste0("modal_", setdiff(names(al_wide), c("file_stem", "allele"))))
cons <- al_wide[cons, on = .(file_stem, allele)]
tract_cols <- paste0("modal_", tracts$tract)
cons[, motif_counts := do.call(paste, c(lapply(tract_cols, function(cc) if (cc %in% names(cons)) round(get(cc)) else NA), sep = "_"))]
cons[, `:=`(left_bp = nchar(consensus_left), mid_bp = nchar(consensus_mid), right_bp = nchar(consensus_right))]
# FASTA: one full-length sequence per allele, and the three parts
cons_dir <- file.path(st_dir, "consensus"); unlink(cons_dir, recursive = TRUE); dir.create(cons_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
hdr <- with(cons, sprintf("%s_allele%d cluster=%d reads=%d share=%.3f %s", file_stem, allele, cluster_number, reads, proportion, repeat_notation))
writeXStringSet(DNAStringSet(setNames(cons$full_sequence, hdr)), file.path(cons_dir, "alleles.fasta"))
if (isTRUE(params$consensus_parts)) for (seg in c("left", "mid", "right")) {
  x <- cons[[paste0("consensus_", seg)]]; ok <- !is.na(x)
  if (any(ok)) writeXStringSet(DNAStringSet(setNames(x[ok], paste0(hdr[ok], "_", seg))), file.path(cons_dir, paste0("alleles_", seg, ".fasta")))
}
timings["Consensus"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

```{r variants, eval=params$cluster && params$call_variants}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
# Variants of each allele: those in its consensus, plus minority substitutions; then the read support of each
reads_by <- split(d_all[, .(file_stem, allele, left, right)], by = c("file_stem", "allele"))
var_list <- apply_fn(seq_len(nrow(cons)), function(i) {
  cc <- cons[i]
  major <- rbind(call_flank_variants(cc$consensus_left, left_ref, 0L), call_flank_variants(cc$consensus_right, right_ref, ref$n_end))
  if (!is.null(major) && nrow(major)) major$in_consensus <- TRUE
  minor <- rbind(minor_variants(cc$consensus_left, cc$minor_left[[1]], left_ref, 0L),
                 minor_variants(cc$consensus_right, cc$minor_right[[1]], right_ref, ref$n_end))
  if (!is.null(minor) && nrow(minor)) {
    minor$in_consensus <- FALSE
    if (!is.null(major) && nrow(major)) minor <- minor[!paste(minor$pos, minor$ref, minor$alt) %in% paste(major$pos, major$ref, major$alt), , drop = FALSE]
  }
  v <- rbind(major, if (!is.null(minor)) unique(minor))
  if (is.null(v) || !nrow(v)) return(NULL)
  rd <- reads_by[[paste(cc$file_stem, cc$allele, sep = ".")]]
  if (nrow(rd) > params$allele_support_reads) { set.seed(123); rd <- rd[sample(.N, params$allele_support_reads)] }
  sup <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(v)), function(j) variant_support(if (v$pos[j] < ref$n_start) rd$left else rd$right, v$alt_context[j], v$ref_context[j]), numeric(3)))
  v <- cbind(v, sup)
  # a minority call is kept only when the reads confirm it
  v <- v[v$in_consensus | (!is.na(v$support) & v$support >= params$allele_minor_share & v$alt_reads >= 3), , drop = FALSE]
  if (!nrow(v)) return(NULL)
  data.table(file_stem = cc$file_stem, allele = cc$allele, cluster_number = cc$cluster_number, v)
})
variants <- rbindlist(var_list)
if (!nrow(variants)) variants <- data.table(file_stem = character(0), allele = integer(0), cluster_number = integer(0), pos = integer(0), ref = character(0),
                                            alt = character(0), type = character(0), alt_context = character(0), ref_context = character(0),
                                            in_consensus = logical(0), alt_reads = numeric(0), ref_reads = numeric(0), support = numeric(0))
n_start_ref <- ref$n_start
variants[, flank := ifelse(pos < n_start_ref, "left", "right")]
# Confirmed by the reads: a consensus variant carried by at least half of the counted reads, or a
# minority variant by at least allele_minor_share. A consensus variant the reads do not confirm
# usually comes from a consensus misaligned around an indel or a repeat; check it in the BAM.
variants[, confirmed := !is.na(support) & support >= ifelse(in_consensus, 0.5, params$allele_minor_share)]
var_counts <- variants[, .(variants_in_consensus = sum(in_consensus), minority_variants = sum(!in_consensus), not_confirmed = sum(!confirmed)), by = .(file_stem, allele)]
cons <- var_counts[cons, on = .(file_stem, allele)][is.na(variants_in_consensus), `:=`(variants_in_consensus = 0L, minority_variants = 0L, not_confirmed = 0L)]
# Read support of every variant in both alleles of its sample, so a heterozygous variant shows
# its support in the allele that carries it and in the one that does not (near 0%)
vk <- unique(variants[allele %in% 1:2, .(file_stem, pos, ref, alt, type, alt_context, ref_context)], by = c("file_stem", "pos", "ref", "alt"))
support_all <- if (nrow(vk)) rbindlist(apply_fn(unique(vk$file_stem), function(s) {
  vs <- vk[file_stem == s]
  rbindlist(lapply(sort(cons[file_stem == s, allele]), function(k) {
    rd <- reads_by[[paste(s, k, sep = ".")]]
    if (is.null(rd)) return(NULL)
    if (nrow(rd) > params$allele_support_reads) { set.seed(123); rd <- rd[sample(.N, params$allele_support_reads)] }
    sup <- t(vapply(seq_len(nrow(vs)), function(j) variant_support(if (vs$pos[j] < n_start_ref) rd$left else rd$right, vs$alt_context[j], vs$ref_context[j]), numeric(3)))
    data.table(file_stem = s, allele = k, vs[, .(pos, ref, alt, type)], sup)
  }))
})) else data.table()
if (nrow(support_all)) {
  support_all <- variants[, .(file_stem, allele, pos, ref, alt, in_consensus, confirmed, carried = TRUE)][support_all, on = .(file_stem, allele, pos, ref, alt)]
  support_all[is.na(carried), `:=`(carried = FALSE, in_consensus = FALSE, confirmed = FALSE)]
}
# Where each extra cluster (allele 3 upwards) comes from. Its length is compared with alleles 1
# and 2, and its flanks are read at the variants that tell alleles 1 and 2 apart (support at
# least 60 points higher in one than the other): the share of its reads with allele 1's base.
# An extra cluster with one allele's length and the other allele's flanks is the signature of a
# PCR chimera (template switching between the alleles during amplification). The other tracts
# (e.g. CCG) are also compared: an extra cluster whose other tract lengths match neither allele
# cannot have come from either and most likely comes from another sample; where alleles 1 and 2
# differ in another tract, that tract tells which allele the extra cluster's reads came from even
# when no flank variant does.
allele_origin <- function(cs, sa, tc = NULL) {
  none <- data.table(file_stem = character(0), allele = integer(0), origin = character(0))
  a12 <- cs[allele %in% 1:2]
  # Nothing to explain without two alleles to compare with, or without an extra cluster.
  # (Before v3.3.2 a sample with exactly two alleles returned a one-row table with no allele
  # column, which stopped the module when every sample had exactly two.)
  if (nrow(a12) < 2 || !any(cs$allele > 2)) return(none)
  near <- function(m, ref_m) abs(m - ref_m) <= max(3, 0.1 * ref_m)
  ph <- if (nrow(sa)) dcast(sa[allele %in% 1:2 & !is.na(support), .(pos, ref, alt, allele, support)], pos + ref + alt ~ allele, value.var = "support") else data.table()
  if (nrow(ph) && all(c("1", "2") %in% names(ph))) { setnames(ph, c("1", "2"), c("s1", "s2")); ph <- ph[!is.na(s1) & !is.na(s2) & abs(s1 - s2) >= 0.6] } else ph <- data.table()
  rbindlist(lapply(cs[allele > 2, allele], function(k) {
    m <- cs[allele == k, modal_length]
    len_like <- c(near(m, a12[allele == 1, modal_length]), near(m, a12[allele == 2, modal_length]))
    len_txt <- if (all(len_like)) "length of alleles 1 and 2" else if (len_like[1]) "allele 1's length" else if (len_like[2]) "allele 2's length" else sprintf("its own length (%s)", m)
    # Other tracts: lengths within 1 unit count as the same
    tr_txt <- ""; tr_a <- NA_integer_
    if (!is.null(tc) && nrow(tc) && all(c(1:2, k) %in% tc$allele)) {
      oth <- intersect(paste0("modal_", setdiff(tracts$tract, primary)), names(tc))
      for (o in oth) {
        x <- tc[allele == k, get(o)]; x1 <- tc[allele == 1, get(o)]; x2 <- tc[allele == 2, get(o)]
        if (anyNA(c(x, x1, x2))) next
        nm <- sub("^modal_", "", o)
        if (abs(x - x1) > 1 && abs(x - x2) > 1) { tr_txt <- sprintf(", its %s length (%s) matches neither allele (%s, %s) – likely from another sample", nm, x, x1, x2); break }
        if (abs(x1 - x2) > 1) { tr_a <- if (abs(x - x1) <= 1) 1L else 2L; tr_txt <- sprintf(", its %s length (%s) is allele %d's", nm, x, tr_a) }
      }
    }
    fl <- if (nrow(ph)) sa[allele == k & !is.na(support), .(pos, ref, alt, support)][ph, on = .(pos, ref, alt), nomatch = NULL] else data.table()
    if (grepl("another sample", tr_txt)) return(data.table(allele = k, origin = paste0(len_txt, tr_txt)))
    if (!nrow(fl)) {
      len_a0 <- if (sum(len_like) == 1) which(len_like) else NA_integer_
      v0 <- if (is.na(tr_a)) "; no variant tells alleles 1 and 2 apart, so its flanks cannot be assigned"
            else if (!is.na(len_a0) && len_a0 != tr_a) " – likely PCR chimera"
            else if (!is.na(len_a0)) sprintf(" – part of allele %d", len_a0)
            else " – a different length on that allele (subclone, smear or contamination)"
      return(data.table(allele = k, origin = paste0(len_txt, tr_txt, v0)))
    }
    fl[, like1 := ifelse(s1 > s2, support, 1 - support)]
    # Per flank: 1 or 2 when nearly every telling variant matches that allele; "other" when each
    # variant clearly matches one allele but not always the same one (a third haplotype); "mixed"
    # when the reads are split at the variants themselves
    cls <- function(v) { a1 <- mean(v >= 0.8); a2 <- mean(v <= 0.2)
      if (a1 >= 0.8) "1" else if (a2 >= 0.8) "2" else if (a1 + a2 >= 0.8) "other" else "mixed" }
    side <- fl[, .(cl = cls(like1)), by = .(side = ifelse(pos < n_start_ref, "left", "right"))]
    num <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(side$cl))
    fl_a <- if (all(!is.na(num)) && length(unique(num)) == 1) num[1] else NA_integer_
    fl_txt <- if (!is.na(fl_a)) sprintf("allele %d's flanks", fl_a)
              else if (all(!is.na(num))) paste(sprintf("%s flank like allele %d", side$side, num), collapse = ", ")
              else if (any(side$cl == "other")) "flanks unlike either allele (they match allele 1 at some variants and allele 2 at others)"
              else "flanks mixed between the two alleles"
    len_a <- if (sum(len_like) == 1) which(len_like) else NA_integer_
    # The other tract and the flanks point to different alleles: a combination neither allele
    # carries, most likely an allele of another sample (contamination)
    verdict <- if (!is.na(tr_a) && !is.na(fl_a) && tr_a != fl_a) " \u2013 its other tract and its flanks point to different alleles: likely from another sample (contamination)"
               else if (!is.na(len_a) && !is.na(fl_a) && len_a != fl_a) " \u2013 likely PCR chimera"
               else if (!is.na(len_a) && !is.na(fl_a)) sprintf(" \u2013 part of allele %d", len_a)
               else if (is.na(len_a) && !is.na(fl_a)) " \u2013 a different length on that allele (subclone, smear or contamination)"
               else if (all(!is.na(num)) && length(unique(num)) > 1) " \u2013 likely PCR chimera (each flank from a different allele)"
               else if (any(side$cl == "other")) " \u2013 a third haplotype: another cell line or a contaminating sample"
               else ""
    data.table(allele = k, origin = paste0(len_txt, tr_txt, ", ", fl_txt, verdict))
  }))[, file_stem := cs$file_stem[1]][]
}
origin <- rbindlist(lapply(split(cluster_summary, by = "file_stem"), function(cs) allele_origin(cs, if (nrow(support_all)) support_all[file_stem == cs$file_stem[1]] else data.table(), cons[file_stem == cs$file_stem[1]])), fill = TRUE)
if (nrow(origin) && all(c("file_stem", "allele", "origin") %in% names(origin))) cons <- origin[cons, on = .(file_stem, allele)] else cons[, origin := NA_character_]
var_dir <- file.path(st_dir, "variants"); unlink(var_dir, recursive = TRUE); dir.create(var_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_allele_vcf(as.data.frame(cons), as.data.frame(support_all), ref, paste(tracts$tract, collapse = "_"), file.path(var_dir, "alleles.vcf"))
var_summary <- variants[, .(alleles_in_consensus = sum(in_consensus), alleles_minority = sum(!in_consensus), alleles_confirmed = sum(confirmed), samples = uniqueN(file_stem),
                            median_support = stats::median(support, na.rm = TRUE)), by = .(pos, ref, alt, type, flank)][order(pos)]
timings["Variants"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

```{r alleles_described, results='asis', eval=params$cluster}
# Built in R (an asis block does not evaluate inline R code)
cat(paste0("**How the alleles are described.** Each sample's two largest clusters are its alleles 1 and 2, numbered by the length of the primary tract, ", (primary), " (allele 1 is the shorter), so the same number means the same kind of allele in every sample; further clusters are numbered 3 upwards. For each allele: its modal length for every measure, and the region between the reference flanks written out in repeat notation from its consensus, e.g. (CAG)17 CAACAGCCGCCA (CCG)7, so the tract lengths and interruptions can be read directly. ", (if (params$cluster && params$call_variants) sprintf("Variants are the differences between an allele's flank consensus and the reference, so each belongs to one allele (they are phased). Each carries its read support: the share of that allele's reads (up to %s per allele) that contain the variant with at least %d bases of its consensus either side, out of those reads that contain either the variant or the reference in that context (the context is widened, up to 60 bases, until the two cannot be confused, which matters for an insertion or deletion in repetitive sequence; a read matching both is not counted). Variants not in an allele's consensus are reported when at least %s of its reads carry them (substitutions only; found in the reads aligned for the consensus and confirmed by the read count). A consensus variant that fewer than half of the counted reads carry is marked not confirmed (column confirmed; FILTER LowSupport in the VCF): it usually comes from a consensus misaligned around an indel or inside a repeat, so check it in the BAM before relying on it.", format(params$allele_support_reads, big.mark = ","), 8L, if (is.na(params$allele_minor_share)) "-" else percent(params$allele_minor_share)) else "")), "\n\n")
```

`r if (params$cluster && params$call_variants && exists("support_all") && nrow(support_all)) paste0("**How to read this.** One row per sample, one column per variant (reference position, reference > alternative bases; a long insertion or deletion is shown by its first bases and its length), one panel per allele. The colour is the variant's read support in that allele: the share of the allele's reads carrying it. Every variant found in either allele of a sample is measured in both, so a tile with a dot is in that allele's consensus, a light tile without a dot is carried by a minority of its reads, and a dark tile is an allele that does not carry it (support near 0%). A grey tile is a variant whose support could not be counted, because no read contained it or the reference with the same surrounding bases (or every read matched both); that usually means the call sits in a misaligned or error-prone stretch, and such calls are marked not confirmed. Each sample's label ends with the ", primary, " length of its alleles 1 and 2 (allele 1 is always the shorter), so a variant bright in the allele 2 panel is on the longer allele. A heterozygous flank SNP shows as bright in one allele's panel and dark in the other, in every sample of a line; a variant at intermediate support in one sample only is worth checking in the BAM.") else if (params$cluster && params$call_variants) "No allele differs from the reference within the flank sequence covered, and no minority variant reached the threshold, so the VCF holds only the repeat record." else ""`

```{r variant_map, eval=params$cluster && params$call_variants && exists("support_all") && nrow(support_all) > 0, fig.width=10, fig.height=if (exists("support_all")) min(30, 3 + 0.2 * uniqueN(support_all$file_stem)) else 4}
lab_v <- short_labels(cons$file_stem)
# Long insertions and deletions are labelled by their first bases and length
short_allele <- function(a) ifelse(nchar(a) > 6, sprintf("%s\u2026 (%d bp)", substr(a, 1, 4), nchar(a)), a)
# Each sample is labelled with the primary tract length of its alleles 1 and 2, so every
# variant can be read as being on the shorter or the longer allele
pm <- paste0("modal_", primary)
len_ab <- if (pm %in% names(cons)) cons[allele %in% 1:2, .(txt = paste(get(pm), collapse = " / ")), by = file_stem] else data.table(file_stem = character(0), txt = character(0))
lab_v2 <- stats::setNames(paste0(lab_v, ifelse(is.na(len_ab$txt[match(names(lab_v), len_ab$file_stem)]), "", paste0("  [", primary, " ", len_ab$txt[match(names(lab_v), len_ab$file_stem)], "]"))), names(lab_v))
vm <- copy(support_all)[allele %in% 1:2][, `:=`(sample = factor(lab_v2[file_stem], levels = rev(unique(lab_v2[sort(unique(cons$file_stem))]))),
                                             vlab = sprintf("%d %s>%s", pos, short_allele(ref), short_allele(alt)),
                                             allele_lab = ifelse(allele == 1, sprintf("Allele 1 (shorter %s)", primary), sprintf("Allele 2 (longer %s)", primary)))]
vm[, vlab := factor(vlab, levels = unique(vm[order(pos)]$vlab))]
if (nrow(vm)) {
  n_s <- uniqueN(vm$sample); n_v <- uniqueN(vm$vlab)
  p_vm <- ggplot(vm, aes(vlab, sample, fill = support)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_point(data = vm[in_consensus == TRUE], size = 0.8, colour = "white") +
    facet_wrap(~ allele_lab, ncol = 2) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1), name = "Read support") +
    labs(x = "Variant (position ref>alt)", y = NULL, title = "Variants in alleles 1 and 2 of every sample",
         subtitle = "Colour = share of the allele's reads with the variant; dot = in its consensus; grey = not countable") +
    theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
                       axis.text.y = element_text(size = if (n_s > 60) 5 else 7), panel.grid = element_blank())
  print(p_vm); save_plot(p_vm, file.path(plots_dir, "variants_by_sample.png"), min(40, 5 + 0.6 * n_v), min(40, 3 + 0.2 * n_s))
}
if (exists("var_summary")) dt_full(var_summary, caption = "Variants across the cohort: alleles carrying each in their consensus or as a minority, samples, and median read support", digits = 3)

```{r allele_bams, eval=params$cluster && isTRUE(params$allele_bam)}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
bam_dir <- file.path(st_dir, "bam"); unlink(bam_dir, recursive = TRUE)
bam_tmp <- file.path(temp_dir, "allele_bam"); dir.create(bam_tmp, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
# Short amplicons (a few hundred bp, mostly repeat) are placed from their flanks; a general
# long-read aligner leaves such reads unmapped or splits them at the repeat
flank_bp <- stats::median(nchar(d_all$left) + nchar(d_all$right), na.rm = TRUE)
bam_method <- if (params$allele_bam_method == "auto") (if (is.finite(flank_bp) && flank_bp < 1000) "flanks" else "minimap2") else params$allele_bam_method
invisible(apply_fn(unique(d_all$file_stem), function(s) {
  d <- d_all[file_stem == s & !is.na(allele)]
  set.seed(123); d <- d[, .SD[sample(.N, min(.N, params$allele_bam_reads))], by = allele]
  d[, hp := allele]
  if (!"molecule_id" %in% names(d)) d <- if (!is.null(read_mol)) read_mol[file_stem == s, .(qname, molecule_id)][d, on = "qname"] else d[, molecule_id := NA_character_]
  if (bam_method == "flanks") write_allele_bam_flanks(d, ref, file.path(bam_dir, paste0(s, ".bam")), bam_tmp)
  else write_allele_bam(d, ref, file.path(bam_dir, paste0(s, ".bam")), params$allele_bam_minimap2, 1L, bam_tmp)
  TRUE
}))
timings["Allele BAMs"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
cat(sprintf("Reads were placed on the reference %s. ", if (bam_method == "flanks") sprintf("from their flanks (allele_bam_method = %s; median flank length %s bp): each flank aligned to its reference flank and the repeat region shown as one insertion at the N block, at position %d", params$allele_bam_method, round(flank_bp), ref$n_start - 1) else sprintf("with minimap2 (%s)", params$allele_bam_minimap2)))
cat(sprintf("Allele BAMs written for %d samples (up to %s reads per allele) to bam/. In IGV, load the reference FASTA, alleles.vcf and a sample's BAM, then group or colour the reads by tag HP to see each allele's reads. The repeat is at %s:%s-%s; paste that into the IGV locus box.\n",
            uniqueN(d_all$file_stem), format(params$allele_bam_reads, big.mark = ","), ref$ref_id,
            format(max(1, ref$n_start - 150), big.mark = ","), format(min(nchar(ref$full), ref$n_end + 150), big.mark = ",")))
```

```{asis, echo=params$cluster}
## Viewing the alleles: BAM, VCF and FASTA

The three standard files are made to be looked at together in a genome browser such as IGV, against the same reference Duke used.

1. **Reference.** In IGV, *Genomes > Load Genome from File* and choose the reference FASTA given to Duke (`path_ref`), the one with the N block where the repeat sits. The BAMs and the VCF use its sequence name and coordinates, so no other reference will line up. IGV indexes the FASTA itself the first time (or run `samtools faidx` on it).
2. **Reads.** *File > Load from File* and choose a sample's BAM from `bam/` (its `.bai` index must be in the same folder). Right-click the reads and choose *Group alignments by > tag* and type `HP`: the reads fall into allele 1, allele 2 and any further alleles, so each flank variant can be seen on the allele that carries it. `XR` holds each read's repeat length and `MI` its molecule (UMI runs), for sorting or colouring.
3. **Variants.** Load `variants/alleles.vcf` the same way: one row per sample, with the phased genotype (allele 1 | allele 2) at each flank variant, and the repeat region as one record whose motif counts are in the MC field.

The repeat itself is N in the reference, so the reads show it as a long insertion there; its sequence is in the repeat notation above and in the FASTA.

**The allele FASTA** (`consensus/alleles.fasta`) holds one full-length consensus sequence per allele per sample, with the sample, allele, reads and repeat notation in each header; with `consensus_parts = TRUE`, `alleles_left.fasta`, `alleles_mid.fasta` and `alleles_right.fasta` hold the three parts as well. Uses: aligning the alleles of several samples to compare their structure; checking primer and probe sites against each allele; loading an allele as its own reference in IGV to view its reads without the N block; and as the sequence to report or deposit for each allele.
```


---

# Waterfall plots

Each figure shows up to `r format(params$waterfall_downsample, big.mark = ",")` reads from one sample, ordered from shortest to longest `r primary` tract, with each base coloured and `r params$waterfall_flank_bp` bp of flank either side. A pure tract gives a regular stripe; interruptions show as vertical lines at a fixed offset from the tract start or end, and sequence variants in the flanks as columns of a different colour. The reads are a random sample (with UMIs and clustering on molecules, one read per kept molecule, so each allele takes up its share of molecules rather than of reads), so each allele appears in proportion to its share and takes up that share of the height. Each y-axis label marks the first read whose tract reaches that length; labels are spread evenly up the plot, so a large allele carries several. One example is shown; all are in `plots/waterfall/waterfall_{sample}.png` (and, with `waterfall_cluster` in `plots`, one per cluster in `plots/waterfall_cluster/`).

```{r waterfall, eval=want_plot("waterfall", params) || want_plot("waterfall_cluster", params), fig.height=8}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
wf_dir <- file.path(plots_dir, "waterfall")
first <- NULL
# With molecules, one read per molecule (at random), so each allele takes up its share of
# molecules rather than of reads, as in the cluster figures
wf_unit <- if (exists("cluster_unit") && cluster_unit == "molecules" && "molecule_id" %in% names(d_all)) "molecules" else "reads"
for (s in samples) {
  d <- d_all[file_stem == s]
  if (wf_unit == "molecules") { set.seed(123); d <- d[d[, .I[sample.int(.N, 1)], by = molecule_id]$V1] }
  d <- as.data.frame(d)
  p <- create_waterfall_plot(d, paste("Waterfall:", s), params$waterfall_flank_bp, params$waterfall_downsample,
                             paste(primary, "length"), unit_word = if (wf_unit == "molecules") "molecules (one read each)" else "reads")
  if (is.null(p)) next
  if (is.null(first)) first <- p
  save_plot(p, plot_path(plots_dir, "waterfall", s), 12, 9)
  if (params$cluster && want_plot("waterfall_cluster", params)) for (k in sort(unique(d$cluster_number))) {
    pk <- create_waterfall_plot(d[d$cluster_number == k, ], sprintf("Waterfall: %s, cluster %d", s, k), params$waterfall_flank_bp,
                                params$waterfall_downsample, paste(primary, "length"), unit_word = if (wf_unit == "molecules") "molecules (one read each)" else "reads")
    if (!is.null(pk)) save_plot(pk, plot_path(plots_dir, "waterfall_cluster", s, sprintf("cluster%02d", k)), 12, 9)
  }
}
timings["Waterfalls"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
if (!is.null(first)) print(first)
```

---

# Save output

```{r save}
module5_output <- list(
  clusters = if (params$cluster) d_all[, .(file_stem, qname, cluster_number, allele, repeat_cluster, haplotype_cluster)] else NULL,
  cluster_summary = if (params$cluster) cluster_summary else NULL,
  alleles = if (params$cluster) cons[, !c("minor_left", "minor_right"), with = FALSE] else NULL,
  variants = if (params$cluster && params$call_variants) variants else NULL,
  variant_support = if (params$cluster && params$call_variants) support_all else NULL, hash = params$module_hash)
output_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "05_allele_structure.RData")
save(module5_output, file = output_path, compression_level = 1)   # level 1: several times faster to write than the default, files slightly larger
# Variant rows carry the modal length of every measure in their allele, so each can be read as
# being on the shorter or the longer allele without looking it up in the alleles sheet
with_len <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || !nrow(x) || is.null(module5_output$alleles)) return(x)
  lc <- c("file_stem", "allele", grep("^modal_", names(module5_output$alleles), value = TRUE))
  module5_output$alleles[, lc, with = FALSE][x, on = .(file_stem, allele)]
}
write_excel_function(list(cluster_summary = module5_output$cluster_summary, alleles = module5_output$alleles,
                          variants = if (!is.null(module5_output$variants)) with_len(module5_output$variants[, !c("alt_context", "ref_context"), with = FALSE]) else NULL,
                          variant_support = if (exists("support_all")) with_len(support_all) else NULL,
                          variants_cohort = if (exists("var_summary")) var_summary else NULL), xlsx_path)
```

```{r diagnostics}
timing_df <- build_timing_table(timings)

  alleles = "One row per allele: modal lengths, repeat notation, consensus sequences, flank coverage", variants = "Variants per allele with read support (full-reference coordinates)",
  variant_support = "Read support of every variant in both alleles of its sample",
```
